result.rationale: The diff shows the migration interpolating user-derived host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from `val.split("\n")` of the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting. Values containing single quotes would break the SQL or allow injection; unescaped string interpolation into raw SQL is a genuine defect verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds an INSERT SQL string with direct interpolation of the host value: `VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)`. If `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), this will break the SQL syntax and could allow SQL injection via the persisted `site_settings` value being migrated. This is verifiably present in the diff (the `execute "INSERT ... '#{h}' ..."` line).
